notes: Identity assessment: supplied text contains the full primary report headed Deescalation Strategies: A Comparison of Techniques for Reducing Commitment to Losing Courses of Action, by Itamar Simonson and Barry M. Staw; Journal of Applied Psychology, 1992, Vol. 77, No. 4, 419–426. These bibliographic details match the assigned original reference. The DOI is not printed in this text, so DOI identity was not independently confirmed. Text includes methods, results, discussion and references. No PDF path was supplied; no acquisition or rendering performed. All three assigned rows have the same study/outcome/comparison description. Each is matched independently to the explicitly named process-accountability versus outcome-accountability planned contrast on printed p. 424, not assigned distinct tests by row order. The p. 5 locator (printed p. 423) begins Allocation of Resources; its analysis continues onto p. 6 (printed p. 424). Manipulation-check contrasts on p. 423 concern perceived evaluation, not the described escalating-commitment allocation outcome; process versus baseline (4.07) and the seven-condition omnibus (4.02) on p. 424 are different comparisons. Analytic model N = 30 + 28 + 25 + 30 + 30 + 24 + 26 = 193 participants, summing the mutually exclusive final conditions in Table 2, for the seven-condition analysis with initial product choice as covariate. The two focal conditions each have 30 participants (30 + 30 = 60 focal-condition participants); 60 is not substituted for the full common-model N used by the reported contrast. No exclusions are described. No d is reported for this contrast. The contrast prints 12.41 with same-test p<.01, but its statistic symbol is OCR-corrupted as /-"(I, 183); no F identity or d conversion is asserted. The numerical statistic is retained with generic metric and confidence false pending glyph verification. Unassigned replication, p and success fields are placeholders; same-test p is preserved only in evidence/notes.
